IServiceCollection registrations must be declared as individual statements rather than fluent chains.

What the Standard says

“register dependencies” — The Standard's configuration example presents each dependency-registration operation as an independently readable statement. The analyser turns that demonstrated composition style into a consistent rule. read it here.
“Simplicity” — The Standard requires code to remain simple for mainstream engineers. Separate registration statements make each lifetime and mapping visible without unpacking a fluent chain. read it here.

Why it matters

Individual registration statements make every service addition independently visible, reviewable, and debuggable. Fluent chains hide the failing registration in a long expression and make later reordering or conditional composition unnecessarily awkward.

Bad code example

services
    .AddSingleton<IStudentBroker, StudentBroker>()
    .AddTransient<IStudentService, StudentService>();

Good code example

services.AddSingleton<IStudentBroker, StudentBroker>();
services.AddTransient<IStudentService, StudentService>();
